title: Keyboard Manager: Remapping Left Alt and Left Ctrl triggers both keys simultaneously

fix_assessment.rationale: An observable failure is reported and a specific investigation boundary is identified. The proposed direction remains conditional on controlled reproduction.

steps: Configure only LeftAlt to LeftCtrl on a disposable Windows11profile and compare OSK highlighting with delivered key state in a test application.
Repeat with the optional reverse mapping, then test release, ordinary Alt shortcuts and an AltGr layout separately.
Record physical source, injected target and application-observed modifier state before changing reset or suppression logic.
prerequisites: Use a disposable test environment and test-owned documents/configuration; preserve existing user data.
reproduce.expected: Applications should receive the configured target behavior with correct release state; any OSK-only discrepancy must be distinguished from genuine combined modifiers or AltGr regression.

actions.label: Reproduce Keyboard Manager modifier visibility behavior

evidence: The report supplies LeftAlt to LeftCtrl, an optional reverse mapping, and an On-Screen Keyboard screenshot showing Alt and Ctrl highlighted.
A later participant confirms the same environment and also reports AltGr becoming LeftAlt.
An OSK highlight alone is not a complete delivered-key trace; current single-key remapping explicitly resets modifier state for lower-level handlers.
judgment.rationale: Source and target modifier visibility may diverge across hook, OSK and application state, with a possible AltGr side effect. Compare actual application shortcut delivery and key-up cleanup before concluding which reset path is wrong; do not treat OSK presentation alone as proof every application receives both modifiers.
judgment.recommended_action: Execute the focused maintainer reproduction before choosing an implementation; the proposal is a hypothesis, not an approved detailed design.

verification: Applications should receive the configured target behavior with correct release state; any OSK-only discrepancy must be distinguished from genuine combined modifiers or AltGr regression.
Retest a matching unaffected control and the originally reported workflow on a current supported build.
